steps.question: Do the 12 human liver samples group by condition (control, treated_a, treated_b), and does any of the 4 replicates in a group depart from its group before any test is fitted?

grounding.reason: Raw counts before a model: blind VST, PCA on the top 500 variable genes and a sample distance heatmap are the prescribed sample-structure QC (R-0033).

steps.name: LRT across three groups plus pairwise Wald contrasts
caveats: 4 replicates per group is below 7, so DESeq2 flags count outliers with NA p-values rather than replacing counts; a gene of interest with NA must have its counts inspected
The LRT answers 'differs anywhere' and does not say which pair differs; do not read an LRT hit as a treated-vs-control effect without the corresponding Wald contrast

Counts are gene-level summaries from Salmon, so per-gene average transcript length offsets cannot be carried; a fold change driven by a shift in isoform usage cannot be separated from one driven by gene-level expression
No fold-change threshold is applied inside the test; if a minimum effect size is later wanted it must be tested with lfcThreshold, not filtered post hoc
steps.context: 12,000 genes x 12 samples, human liver, raw Salmon gene-level counts. Groups: control (n=4), treated_a (n=4), treated_b (n=4). Unpaired, single batch, no covariates. The counts are already gene-level, so tximport length offsets are not available — state this and its consequence for isoform-usage-driven fold changes.
steps.question: Which genes differ between any of control, treated_a and treated_b (omnibus), and which genes change in treated_a vs control and in treated_b vs control?

grounding.reason: Three replicated groups, no interaction and no time course: R-0059 prescribes the DESeq2 LRT (~condition vs ~1) for the any-difference question followed by named Wald contrasts against an explicit reference level (R-0060, R-0036), with ashr shrinkage because a non-reference contrast is not one coefficient (R-0040), minimal pre-filter (R-0029/R-0002) and BH within contrast at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering (R-0061, R-0010, R-0043). The reference level is set to 'control' as the concrete instance of the sourced 'explicit' policy.

constraints: Do not pre-normalize, scale or transform the counts before DESeq2; median-of-ratios size factors are estimated inside the model
Pre-filter is minimal: at least 10 counts in at least 4 samples; do not raise the threshold
Set the reference level explicitly with relevel(condition, ref='control') and report it

Use ashr for lfcShrink, not apeglm
BH adjustment within each contrast; state that FDR control holds per contrast and not across the set of contrasts
Pass alpha = 0.05 to results() so independent filtering is optimized for the reporting cutoff

steps.description: On the raw counts, pre-filter genes to those with at least 10 counts in at least 4 samples (the smallest group size), then fit DESeq2 with design ~ condition. Set control as the explicit reference level with relevel before fitting; do not rely on alphabetical ordering. (1) Omnibus: run the likelihood ratio test with full = ~ condition and reduced = ~ 1 to obtain the genes that differ across any of the three groups. (2) Pairwise: extract named Wald contrasts c('condition','treated_a','control') and c('condition','treated_b','control'), and additionally c('condition','treated_b','treated_a') as a secondary comparison. Apply ashr shrinkage to each contrast's log2 fold change (ashr, not apeglm, because a non-reference contrast is not a single coefficient) and keep both the unshrunken estimate with its lfcSE and the shrunken estimate in every table. Adjust p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg within each contrast and within the LRT separately, at alpha 0.05, with DESeq2 independent filtering left on and the same alpha passed to results(). Plot the unadjusted p-value histogram for the LRT and for each contrast before trusting the adjusted values. Leave Cook's-distance outlier flagging on and report the number of genes with NA p-values from outlier flagging separately from those set NA by independent filtering. Write one results table per contrast plus the LRT table, each labelled with its contrast name, and the normalized (median-of-ratios) count matrix.

steps.name: edgeR quasi-likelihood robustness check
caveats: Disagreement between the two methods grows at low counts and at low replicate numbers, so a gene called by only one method at n=4 per group is a weak call, not a contradiction

steps.context: Same 12,000 x 12 human liver Salmon count matrix and same three-group design as T1S2. edgeR 4.10.3 is installed. This step exists to quantify method dependence at 4 replicates per group, where DESeq2 and edgeR are known to disagree on a minority of genes, particularly at low counts.
steps.question: Do the genes called differential across the three groups and in each treatment-vs-control contrast reproduce under a second method (edgeR quasi-likelihood) on the same counts and design?

grounding.reason: R-0042 requires reporting the overlap of DESeq2 and edgeR QL on the same counts and design as the robustness check, with the intersection as the high-confidence set; R-0059 names the edgeR QL F-test on the condition coefficients as the second method for the omnibus question.

constraints: Use the identical gene filter and identical design as T1S2 so the comparison is like for like
TMM normalization factors inside the edgeR model; do not pre-scale the counts
Report the overlap and the disagreement per comparison; label the method behind every method-unique gene
steps.description: On the same pre-filtered count matrix and the same design ~ condition (control as reference), fit an edgeR quasi-likelihood model: TMM normalization factors, estimateDisp, glmQLFit. Run (1) an ANOVA-like quasi-likelihood F-test on the full set of condition coefficients as the edgeR analogue of the omnibus LRT, and (2) a QL F-test for each of treated_a vs control and treated_b vs control. Adjust with BH within each test. Then compare against the DESeq2 results from T1S2: report the number of significant genes from each method per comparison, the size of the intersection, and the genes each method calls alone, naming the method for each unique set. Present the intersection as the high-confidence set and the method-unique calls as a secondary set. Do not present the union as the result.
acceptance_criteria: edgeR QL F-test results for the omnibus (all condition coefficients) and for treated_a_vs_control and treated_b_vs_control, each BH-adjusted at 0.05
Per-comparison table of: n significant by DESeq2, n significant by edgeR, n in the intersection, n unique to each method

Statement that the union is not reported as the result

The reference store holds MSigDB human hallmark sets (h.all, 2026.1, HGNC symbols) and human WikiPathways (2026.07.10 GMT, HGNC symbols, first field '%'-delimited — split it to recover a readable set name). No KEGG collection is available and none should be fetched.
steps.question: Which pathways are coordinately shifted in treated_a vs control and in treated_b vs control, and which of those are shared between the two treatments?

grounding.reason: Ranked fgsea on the full tested list is the default enrichment method (R-0107, R-0045); human data takes Hallmark first then Reactome and WikiPathways from the store, each with its release stated and kept separate (R-0048, R-0098, R-0165); enrichment runs once per contrast (R-0104). For the disputed ranking metric (R-0108) the Wald statistic side is chosen and stated.

constraints: Rank by the DESeq2 Wald statistic ('stat'); this is the stated choice for the disputed ranking metric, chosen because it scales the effect by its standard error, unlike the unshrunken log2 fold change, and does not produce ties like a signed p-value
Give fgsea the full ranked list of all tested genes; never cut the list by padj or fold change before the test

Universe is the genes tested in T1S2, not the whole genome or the whole annotation
State the release of each collection beside its name in every output
Set and record a random seed for the fgsea permutations
Do not run an over-representation test on a significant-gene list shorter than about 50 genes; the ranked test on the full list is the method here
Resolve gene set collections from the environment's reference store by what the data is; do not hardcode a path that was not confirmed at run time
steps.description: For each of the treated_a_vs_control and treated_b_vs_control contrasts from T1S2 (and treated_b_vs_treated_a as secondary), build a ranked list of every tested gene using the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the 'stat' column) — do not threshold the list first. Run fgsea against three human gene set collections, kept separate and never merged: MSigDB Hallmark first, then a Reactome pathway collection and the human WikiPathways collection from the reference store. Restrict each collection to sets with 15 to 500 members among the tested genes, applied after intersecting each set with the tested genes. Use BH adjustment within each collection and each contrast. Collapse redundant significant sets into groups and report one representative per group with the full table kept as a supplement. Record and report, per collection: its release/version, the number of sets tested after the size window, and the share of tested gene symbols that failed to map into the collection's identifier space. Report leading-edge genes for every significant set, with each member's Wald statistic, and mark leading-edge overlap between reported sets. Finally, tabulate which sets are significant in both treatment contrasts and which are specific to one, keeping the per-contrast tables separate.
acceptance_criteria: One fgsea result table per contrast per collection, each labelled with the contrast name and the collection name and release
Ranking metric stated explicitly as the DESeq2 Wald statistic, with the full tested-gene list used and no pre-thresholding

steps.name: Consolidated report
caveats: An LRT hit without a significant pairwise contrast means the omnibus test detected a difference the individual contrasts are underpowered to localize at n=4 per group — say so rather than assigning it to a treatment
Sets appearing in both Hallmark and another collection are one finding, not two
steps.context: Final synthesis step for the three-group human liver bulk RNA-seq analysis. It produces the answer to both halves of the research question: the omnibus LRT gene set (differs across the three groups at all) and the per-treatment contrast gene sets (treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control), plus the secondary treated_b vs treated_a comparison.
steps.question: What is the reproducible summary of which genes differ across control, treated_a and treated_b, and which genes each treatment changes relative to control, with the evidence and its limits stated?

grounding.reason: Report content follows the procedure's report step: method/versions/design/thresholds/n_tested/n_de (R-0041), MA and dispersion diagnostics (R-0087), shrunken and unshrunken LFC with lfcSE and ranking on the shrunken value (R-0085), two-method overlap (R-0042), enrichment provenance and method-dependence caveat (R-0051, R-0055), leading edge per set (R-0105), and the reproducibility record (R-0086).

constraints: Report both the shrunken and the unshrunken log2 fold change with the lfcSE; never rank by the unshrunken value alone
Name the shrinkage estimator (ashr) in the table header
Keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit; shrinkage does not change the test
Label every gene list and every adjusted p-value with its contrast
Do not present enrichment sets as proven findings; state method dependence
Store the reproducibility record with the results, not as a separate note
steps.description: Assemble a single report from T1S2, T1S3 and T2S1. Before the gene tables, state: the methods and every package version, the design formula ~ condition with control as reference, every named contrast, the padj cutoff of 0.05, the number of genes tested after filtering, and the number of DE genes per contrast and for the LRT. Include the two fit diagnostics — the MA plot per contrast with significant genes marked, and the DESeq2 dispersion plot — before the tables, each with a sentence on what it shows. Attach the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, the random seeds used, all package versions, and the version of each gene set collection. State the sample size (4 per group) and that a null result for a contrast is not evidence of no effect.

MA plot per contrast and the DESeq2 dispersion plot, each captioned with what it shows, placed before the gene tables
Gene tables carrying unshrunken log2FoldChange, ashr-shrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, pvalue, padj, and the contrast label
Genes ranked and plotted by the shrunken log2 fold change
High-confidence DESeq2-edgeR intersection reported per comparison alongside method-unique calls
Enrichment section stating collection, release, rank metric, universe, size window, tool version and multiple-testing method, with leading-edge genes per significant set
Explicit statement that FDR control holds within each contrast, not across contrasts
Reproducibility record: sessionInfo, seeds, package versions, gene set collection versions

plan.title: Liver 3-group DE: treated_a and treated_b vs control
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a single 12,000 x 12 raw Salmon gene-level count matrix (counts.csv, gene symbols in column 1) with a 12 x 2 sample table (metadata.csv) declaring three conditions — control, treated_a, treated_b — at 4 human liver replicates each, unpaired, single batch. The research question has two parts and the design answers them in the order the DESeq2 multi-group procedure prescribes. Part one, 'which genes differ across the three groups at all', is an omnibus question that spans more than one model coefficient, so it is answered by a likelihood ratio test of the full design ~condition against the reduced design ~1 — a Wald test on one coefficient cannot answer it. Part two, 'which genes does each treatment change relative to control', is answered by named Wald contrasts (condition, treated_a, control) and (condition, treated_b, control), with control set as an explicit reference level rather than left to alphabetical ordering; the treated_b vs treated_a contrast is reported as a secondary comparison since it is a contrast of two non-reference coefficients. Because a non-reference contrast is not a single coefficient, fold-change shrinkage uses ashr rather than apeglm, and both the shrunken and unshrunken log2 fold changes are carried in the gene table. BH adjustment is applied within each contrast at alpha 0.05 with DESeq2 independent filtering left on; the FDR therefore holds per contrast and every gene list is labelled with its contrast. At 4 replicates per group DESeq2 flags Cook's-distance count outliers with NA p-values rather than replacing counts, so those NAs are counted and reported separately from independent-filtering NAs. QC precedes the model: blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap and library sizes, so that a departing sample is seen before any test. An edgeR quasi-likelihood run on the same filtered matrix and the same design gives the robustness check; the intersection is the high-confidence set and method-unique calls are reported separately, never as a union. Enrichment runs once per contrast on the full ranked list of tested genes using the DESeq2 Wald statistic as the ranking metric (the disputed choice is stated: the Wald statistic, being scaled by its standard error, avoids the noisy large fold changes of low-count genes and the rank ties of a signed p-value), against MSigDB Hallmark first and then Reactome and WikiPathways human as separate collections, each with its release stated and never merged. The counts are gene-level and already summarised from Salmon, so tximport length offsets cannot be applied here — that limitation is stated rather than worked around, and it means a fold change driven by isoform-usage change cannot be distinguished from one driven by gene-level expression. Caveat throughout: 4 per group is adequate for DESeq2/edgeR FDR control but modest in power, and a null result for a contrast is not evidence of no effect.

fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic, per contrast, Hallmark then Reactome and WikiPathways
Consolidated report: design, thresholds, MA and dispersion plots, shrunken and unshrunken LFC, leading edge genes, sessionInfo

steps.name: edgeR quasi-likelihood robustness check
steps.question: Do the genes called differential across the three groups and in each treatment-vs-control contrast reproduce under a second method (edgeR quasi-likelihood) on the same counts and design?
steps.description: On the same pre-filtered count matrix and the same design ~ condition (control as reference), fit an edgeR quasi-likelihood model: TMM normalization factors, estimateDisp, glmQLFit. Run (1) an ANOVA-like quasi-likelihood F-test on the full set of condition coefficients as the edgeR analogue of the omnibus LRT, and (2) a QL F-test for each of treated_a vs control and treated_b vs control. Adjust with BH within each test. Then compare against the DESeq2 results from T1S2: report the number of significant genes from each method per comparison, the size of the intersection, and the genes each method calls alone, naming the method for each unique set. Present the intersection as the high-confidence set and the method-unique calls as a secondary set. Do not present the union as the result.
steps.context: Same 12,000 x 12 human liver Salmon count matrix and same three-group design as T1S2. edgeR 4.10.3 is installed. This step exists to quantify method dependence at 4 replicates per group, where DESeq2 and edgeR are known to disagree on a minority of genes, particularly at low counts.
acceptance_criteria: edgeR QL F-test results for the omnibus (all condition coefficients) and for treated_a_vs_control and treated_b_vs_control, each BH-adjusted at 0.05
Per-comparison table of: n significant by DESeq2, n significant by edgeR, n in the intersection, n unique to each method
Explicit high-confidence gene set defined as the DESeq2-edgeR intersection per comparison, written out
Statement that the union is not reported as the result
constraints: Use the identical gene filter and identical design as T1S2 so the comparison is like for like
TMM normalization factors inside the edgeR model; do not pre-scale the counts
Report the overlap and the disagreement per comparison; label the method behind every method-unique gene
caveats: Disagreement between the two methods grows at low counts and at low replicate numbers, so a gene called by only one method at n=4 per group is a weak call, not a contradiction
edgeR's omnibus F-test and DESeq2's LRT are analogous but not identical tests; a difference in their gene counts is expected and is not itself evidence of an error

grounding.reason: R-0042 requires reporting the overlap of DESeq2 and edgeR QL on the same counts and design as the robustness check, with the intersection as the high-confidence set; R-0059 names the edgeR QL F-test on the condition coefficients as the second method for the omnibus question.

steps.name: Preranked GSEA per contrast
steps.question: Which pathways are coordinately shifted in treated_a vs control and in treated_b vs control, and which of those are shared between the two treatments?
steps.description: For each of the treated_a_vs_control and treated_b_vs_control contrasts from T1S2 (and treated_b_vs_treated_a as secondary), build a ranked list of every tested gene using the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the 'stat' column) — do not threshold the list first. Run fgsea against three human gene set collections, kept separate and never merged: MSigDB Hallmark first, then a Reactome pathway collection and the human WikiPathways collection from the reference store. Restrict each collection to sets with 15 to 500 members among the tested genes, applied after intersecting each set with the tested genes. Use BH adjustment within each collection and each contrast. Collapse redundant significant sets into groups and report one representative per group with the full table kept as a supplement. Record and report, per collection: its release/version, the number of sets tested after the size window, and the share of tested gene symbols that failed to map into the collection's identifier space. Report leading-edge genes for every significant set, with each member's Wald statistic, and mark leading-edge overlap between reported sets. Finally, tabulate which sets are significant in both treatment contrasts and which are specific to one, keeping the per-contrast tables separate.
steps.context: Human liver, gene symbols as identifiers in the input matrix. The reference store holds MSigDB human hallmark sets (h.all, 2026.1, HGNC symbols) and human WikiPathways (2026.07.10 GMT, HGNC symbols, first field '%'-delimited — split it to recover a readable set name). A Reactome collection should be resolved from the store by what it is (a human Reactome pathway gene set collection); if no Reactome collection is present at run time, run Hallmark and WikiPathways, and state in the output that Reactome was unavailable rather than substituting another collection. No KEGG collection is available and none should be fetched.
acceptance_criteria: One fgsea result table per contrast per collection, each labelled with the contrast name and the collection name and release
Ranking metric stated explicitly as the DESeq2 Wald statistic, with the full tested-gene list used and no pre-thresholding
Gene set size window of 15-500 applied after intersection with tested genes, and the number of sets tested reported per collection
Share of tested gene symbols unmapped to each collection reported
Leading-edge genes listed for each significant set with their Wald statistics, and overlap between reported sets marked
Redundant significant sets collapsed, with one representative per group in the headline table and the full table retained
Cross-contrast summary naming sets significant in both treated_a and treated_b vs control and those specific to one
constraints: Rank by the DESeq2 Wald statistic ('stat'); this is the stated choice for the disputed ranking metric, chosen because it scales the effect by its standard error, unlike the unshrunken log2 fold change, and does not produce ties like a signed p-value
Give fgsea the full ranked list of all tested genes; never cut the list by padj or fold change before the test
Run enrichment once per contrast; never pool genes from different contrasts into one list
Keep the collections separate — do not merge Hallmark, Reactome and WikiPathways into a single set list
Universe is the genes tested in T1S2, not the whole genome or the whole annotation
State the release of each collection beside its name in every output
Set and record a random seed for the fgsea permutations
Do not run an over-representation test on a significant-gene list shorter than about 50 genes; the ranked test on the full list is the method here
Resolve gene set collections from the environment's reference store by what the data is; do not hardcode a path that was not confirmed at run time
caveats: Enrichment results depend strongly on the method and on the collection; present each set as a hypothesis for follow-up, not as a proven finding
Gene length and expression level bias detection in count data, which propagates into enrichment; the tested-gene universe removes only the detection part of this bias
A pathway present in two collections is one finding tested twice — do not count it twice in the summary
If the Reactome collection is absent from the reference store at run time, report the gap explicitly; the analysis still stands on Hallmark and WikiPathways

grounding.reason: Ranked fgsea on the full tested list is the default enrichment method (R-0107, R-0045); human data takes Hallmark first then Reactome and WikiPathways from the store, each with its release stated and kept separate (R-0048, R-0098, R-0165); enrichment runs once per contrast (R-0104). For the disputed ranking metric (R-0108) the Wald statistic side is chosen and stated.

steps.name: Consolidated report
steps.question: What is the reproducible summary of which genes differ across control, treated_a and treated_b, and which genes each treatment changes relative to control, with the evidence and its limits stated?
steps.description: Assemble a single report from T1S2, T1S3 and T2S1. Before the gene tables, state: the methods and every package version, the design formula ~ condition with control as reference, every named contrast, the padj cutoff of 0.05, the number of genes tested after filtering, and the number of DE genes per contrast and for the LRT. Include the two fit diagnostics — the MA plot per contrast with significant genes marked, and the DESeq2 dispersion plot — before the tables, each with a sentence on what it shows. Gene tables carry, for every gene, the unshrunken log2FoldChange, the ashr-shrunken log2FoldChange, the lfcSE, the p-value and the BH padj, with the contrast named in the table; rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken value, never on the unshrunken value alone. Present the DESeq2-edgeR intersection as the high-confidence set with the method-unique calls beside it. For the enrichment, report the collection, its release, the ranking metric (Wald statistic), the universe (tested genes), the size window (15-500), the tool and its version, the multiple-testing method, and the leading-edge genes of each significant set; state that enrichment results are method-dependent. Attach the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, the random seeds used, all package versions, and the version of each gene set collection. State the sample size (4 per group) and that a null result for a contrast is not evidence of no effect.
steps.context: Final synthesis step for the three-group human liver bulk RNA-seq analysis. It produces the answer to both halves of the research question: the omnibus LRT gene set (differs across the three groups at all) and the per-treatment contrast gene sets (treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control), plus the secondary treated_b vs treated_a comparison.
acceptance_criteria: Header block naming method, package versions, design formula, reference level, every contrast, thresholds, n genes tested, n DE per contrast and for the LRT
MA plot per contrast and the DESeq2 dispersion plot, each captioned with what it shows, placed before the gene tables
Gene tables carrying unshrunken log2FoldChange, ashr-shrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, pvalue, padj, and the contrast label
Genes ranked and plotted by the shrunken log2 fold change
High-confidence DESeq2-edgeR intersection reported per comparison alongside method-unique calls
Enrichment section stating collection, release, rank metric, universe, size window, tool version and multiple-testing method, with leading-edge genes per significant set
Explicit statement that FDR control holds within each contrast, not across contrasts
Reproducibility record: sessionInfo, seeds, package versions, gene set collection versions
Explicit power and limitation statement covering n=4 per group, gene-level counts without length offsets, and the LRT-vs-contrast distinction
constraints: Report both the shrunken and the unshrunken log2 fold change with the lfcSE; never rank by the unshrunken value alone
Name the shrinkage estimator (ashr) in the table header
Keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit; shrinkage does not change the test
Label every gene list and every adjusted p-value with its contrast
Do not present enrichment sets as proven findings; state method dependence
Store the reproducibility record with the results, not as a separate note
caveats: An LRT hit without a significant pairwise contrast means the omnibus test detected a difference the individual contrasts are underpowered to localize at n=4 per group — say so rather than assigning it to a treatment
Sets appearing in both Hallmark and another collection are one finding, not two

grounding.reason: Report content follows the procedure's report step: method/versions/design/thresholds/n_tested/n_de (R-0041), MA and dispersion diagnostics (R-0087), shrunken and unshrunken LFC with lfcSE and ranking on the shrunken value (R-0085), two-method overlap (R-0042), enrichment provenance and method-dependence caveat (R-0051, R-0055), leading edge per set (R-0105), and the reproducibility record (R-0086).
